meta.verified_for_version_note: A full current-documentation audit was performed for v3.15.7. The paths Nexus-Hub currently writes remain functional, so contract_checks and install_verify are unchanged. The audit found additive native agent and hook capabilities that Nexus-Hub does not yet deliver; the maintainer approved documenting that drift and implementing it in v3.15.8 rather than expanding v3.15.7. The non-consumed release_verification_v3_15_7 block records MATCH, DRIFT-ADDITIVE, and UNVERIFIED findings without promising adapter behavior that has not landed.
meta.description: Machine-readable single source for the platform read-contract guards. The human-readable surface table, formats, and source URLs live alongside in platform-read-contracts.md. Consumed by: scripts/verify_platform_contracts.py (contract_checks, code-vs-contract), scripts/lib/integrations/runner.py _verify_checks (install_verify, install-vs-reality), and scripts/check_platform_contract_freshness.py (meta, the release freshness gate). Re-verified against each platform's current docs and re-stamped (last_verified + verified_for_version) at every /update release by the platform-contract-verification skill.
meta.path_tokens: In install_verify paths, '~/' resolves to the user home and '{project}/' resolves to the workspace/target root.

parity_verification_v3_15_0._comment: Phase 1.2 of the v3.15.0 platform-parity release. Web re-verified (2026-07-20) the additive surfaces the 2026-07-19 (v3.14.5) re-verification log deferred to v3.15.0. This block is a findings record only; it is NOT consumed by any guard. contract_checks / install_verify rows and the verified_for_version re-stamp to 3.15.0 are added per phase AS the integration code that satisfies them lands (adding a contract_checks row before its integration writes the surface would fail verify_platform_contracts.py). The gemini_cli_class + decision fields for qwen and kimi are the Phase 4 reclassification go/no-go gate (sub-task 1.3).

cursor.note: Cursor 2.4 gained Skills, Subagents, and Hooks; Rules unchanged. Skills discovery is RECURSIVE (nested and flattened both work). Subagent files are plain .md with frontmatter, NOT .agent.md. The global ~/.cursor/commands/ path (baseline) is UNVERIFIED against reachable docs; project .cursor/commands/<name>.md is confirmed.

hooks.format: hooks.json: {version:1, hooks:{<event>:[{command}]}}; events incl beforeShellExecution/afterShellExecution/afterFileEdit/preToolUse/postToolUse/sessionStart/stop; exit 0 ok, 2 block, other fail-open; matcher supported
hooks.phase2_resolved: 2026-07-21 (Phase 2): cursor.com/docs/hooks confirms {version:1, hooks:{<event>:[{command}]}}; type/timeout/loop_limit/failClosed/matcher are all OPTIONAL (defaults type=command, failClosed=false, loop_limit=5). The minimal git-guardrails writer (beforeShellExecution -> {command}, exit 2 blocks) is schema-valid and needs no change. DF-1(b) resolved.

commands.phase2_note: 2026-07-21 (Phase 2): project .cursor/commands/<name>.md re-confirmed (documented since Cursor 1.6); global ~/.cursor/commands remains UNVERIFIED (no official doc reachable; forum.cursor.com reports it as an open feature-request, not a built-in). Global write retained per plan 2.3 (harmless if unread; negative-only evidence); tracked as known-gap DF-1 residual. Project .cursor/commands/ now also seeded by nexus-hub init (wire_project_surfaces).

opencode.note: Agents folder is new; a plugins/hooks mechanism exists but is a JS/TS (Bun) runtime that Nexus-Hub's shell/python hook scripts cannot drop into. Skills, commands, rules unchanged.

agents.phase3_delivered: 2026-07-21: shipped via the agents_subdir config; the base _mirror_catalog copies catalog/agents/*.md verbatim to both scopes. OpenCode reads .md + frontmatter with mode defaulting to all, and ignores the non-native name/tools keys, so the catalog personas load as-is.

plugins_hooks.format: JS/TS module (Bun); event API, not shell/py hooks
plugins_hooks.phase3_decision: OUT-OF-SCOPE (Phase 3.2, 2026-07-21): re-confirmed plugins are JS/TS Bun modules exporting event hooks; a .sh/.py hook cannot be dropped in and run. hooks_supported stays False; DF-4 resolved as a documented non-gap.

rules.note: No rules/ folder; AGENTS.md + instructions[] array

qwen.note: Qwen Code is an open-source Gemini CLI fork; reproduces skills + commands + agents under ~/.qwen / .qwen. Reclassify in Phase 4. Caveat: open issue #2343 reports project-scoped skills may not auto-load on some builds; a live smoke test is prudent before shipping.
qwen.phase4_delivered: 2026-07-21 (Phase 4): reclassified to SkillsIntegration. Delivers flattened skills + agents + MARKDOWN commands (TOML is deprecated per the docs, so NOT used) at ~/.qwen/{skills,agents,commands} (global, detection-gated) and .qwen/{skills,agents,commands} (project), preserving the QWEN.md write. Skills delivered to BOTH scopes to mitigate DF-2 (#2343 project auto-load); docs confirm a restart loads them.

skills.format: folder-per-skill SKILL.md, one level, name+description frontmatter

commands.format: Markdown primary; TOML (description+prompt) deprecated-but-supported, matches Gemini CLI

rules.note: QWEN.md context file; no rules/ folder

kimi.note: CRITICAL: the current product is Kimi Code CLI (MoonshotAI/kimi-code, data root ~/.kimi-code/), NOT the deprecated old Kimi CLI (~/.kimi/) the baseline targets. Kimi Code CLI reads a folder-per-skill SKILL.md tree and exposes skills as slash commands; there is NO separate command file format (commands == skills; commands.html 404s) and NO user-definable agents surface. Drop the baseline .kimi/agent.yaml (unsupported in the new product). Phase 4 should resolve old ~/.kimi/ vs new ~/.kimi-code/ vs the cross-tool .agents/skills/.
kimi.phase4_delivered: 2026-07-21 (Phase 4): reclassified to SkillsIntegration and FULLY MIGRATED to Kimi Code CLI (~/.kimi-code) per the maintainer decision. Delivers AGENTS.md + flattened skills (incl. command-skills, which reach Kimi as /skill:<name>) at ~/.kimi-code/ (global, detection-gated) and .kimi-code/ (project). Writes only the NATIVE ~/.kimi-code/skills (not the shared ~/.agents/skills, to avoid a teardown conflict with codex). The old ~/.kimi/ writes and the .kimi/agent.yaml companion are DROPPED (neither is read by the current product). No agents surface (Kimi has only built-ins); hooks are config.toml [[hooks]] (out of scope).

skills.format: folder-per-skill SKILL.md (or flat <name>.md), one level; does NOT scan ~/.claude/skills in the new product

commands.note: No standalone command format; each skill auto-registers as /skill:<name>

agents.note: Only 3 fixed built-in subagents; no user-definable agent files

hooks.note: [[hooks]] TOML array in ~/.kimi-code/config.toml; config-merge, not folder-copy

instruction.note: ~/.kimi-code/AGENTS.md (global), .kimi-code/AGENTS.md or AGENTS.md (project); baseline's ~/.kimi/ is the deprecated product

copilot.note: Skills are now a native, default-on surface (VS Code confirmed; GitHub docs do not contradict); the .github/skills path MATCHES baseline but the opt-in/env-gated/off-by-default framing is stale. Custom agents and hooks (Preview) are new. Phase 5: .github/skills commit-visibility remains a Nexus-Hub policy consideration (keep never-overwrite), even though Copilot no longer technically requires opt-in.
copilot.phase5_delivered: 2026-07-21 (Phase 5): the .github/skills seeding was widened from a bare on/off toggle to a SELECTOR - NEXUS_HUB_COPILOT_SKILLS now accepts a bundle id (any of data/bundles.json) or 'all' (full catalog), with bare-truthy still meaning the default core-developer bundle. Kept OFF by default and never-overwrite (the .github/skills path is commit-visible - a Nexus-Hub policy choice, not a Copilot requirement, since Copilot reads skills natively default-on). The stale opt-in FRAMING is corrected in copilot.py's docstring. DF-5 resolved.

release_verification_v3_15_7._comment: Release-time findings only. This block is NOT consumed by any guard. contract_checks and install_verify continue to describe delivered behavior and must change only when matching adapter and test changes land.

codex.resolved_in: 3.15.8 Phase 5. Re-verified 2026-08-02 against the official subagents and hooks references: custom agents are standalone TOML (name, description, developer_instructions required) at ~/.codex/agents and .codex/agents, and hooks.json sits beside an active config layer with the same event names Nexus-Hub already uses. Both are now delivered, so this DRIFT-ADDITIVE finding is closed.
